title: Prime Minister participates in the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), held in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, between August 31 - September 01, 2026.
This year marks SCO’s 25th anniversary. On this occasion, the leaders took stock of the progress and exchanged views on furthering SCO’s role for peace, security, stability and prosperity in the region.
Prime Minister began his address by thanking the President of the Kyrgyz Republic, H.E. Mr. Sadyr Zhaparov for his warmth and hospitality. He noted that the 25th anniversary of the Summit was an opportune time to lay the roadmap for the next 25 years, building upon the strong tradition of dialogue and cooperation developed by SCO. He stated that in the last Summit, India had shared its vision of Security, Connectivity and Opportunity, and now the group must work to realise concrete outcomes in these three pillars of joint work. He reiterated India’s position that conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield and dialogue and diplomacy are the only way forward. Highlighting that terrorism was a grave threat to humanity, he called for committed action to dismantle the terror ecosystem. He specifically stressed that there should be no double standards whatsoever in fight against terrorism. Noting that security in the Eurasia region was closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan, he highlighted India’s development and humanitarian assistance to the country.
Prime Minister further stated that strong and trusted connectivity initiatives were important for the group’s shared progress and prosperity. Underlining that India supports connectivity efforts that link markets, enhance trade and open new opportunities for development, he reiterated that such efforts should respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of nations. He further elaborated that technology, entrepreneurship, innovation, start-ups and people-to-people initiatives open immense opportunities for people in the SCO countries. In this regard, he appreciated the focus on youth engagement under Kyrgyzstan’s presidency. Prime Minister underscored that India would be delighted to host the first edition of the SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum, later this year. This has been India’s flagship initiative seeking to forge civilisational exchanges among the member states.
Besides the Bishkek Declaration, four MoUs, and over twenty decisions and statements were adopted at the Summit in fields ranging from climate, nuclear safety, energy conservation, and combating drug addiction.
India led and supported several initiatives which find place in the Bishkek Declaration, such as English in SCO Charter as the Official Language; Civilization Dialogue Forum; Young Scientist Forum; and Young Author’s Conclave.
Prime Minister thanked President H.E. Sadyr Jhaparov for the successful organization of the Summit. He expressed India’s commitment to work with the SCO family for shared progress and prosperity.

title: English Translation of Prime Minister’s Statement at the 26th SCO Summit
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 1:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
President of Kyrgyzstan,
Excellencies,
Namaskar!
It is a matter of great pleasure for me to be here amongst all of you on this special occasion of the 25th anniversary of the SCO.
I sincerely thank President Japarov for the warm welcome and gracious hospitality extended to us in Bishkek.
We had the privilege of being here yesterday, on the occasion of Kyrgyzstan’s Independence Day. I once again extend my warmest congratulations to the President and the people of Kyrgyzstan.
And today, on the occasion of Uzbekistan’s Independence Day, I extend my warmest congratulations to the President and the people of Uzbekistan as well.
During the spectacular Opening Ceremony of the World Nomad Games, we all caught a glimpse of Kyrgyzstan’s rich culture and our shared heritage. This shared heritage and our deep people-to-people connections are among the great strengths of the SCO family.
Friends,
Over the past twenty-five years, the SCO has developed a strong tradition of dialogue and cooperation across the vast expanse of Eurasia. Together, we have made valuable contributions not only to the well-being of our people, but also to the advancement of humanity. Over these twenty-five years, we have laid a strong foundation for cooperation. In the next twenty-five years, our goal should be to translate this cooperation into tangible outcomes.
At a time when the world is passing through uncertainty and instability, we must transform our shared geography into shared opportunities. And through our efforts, we must bring about positive change in the lives of our people.
Friends,
At the previous meeting, I had outlined the three main pillars of India’s vision for the SCO:
S - Security,
C – Connectivity, and
O – Opportunity
The time has come to move these three pillars beyond vision and translate them into concrete outcomes. The first and foremost requirement for this is peace and security. Terrorism continues to pose a serious challenge to humanity as a whole. In the fight against terrorism, we cannot remain confined to an action-reaction approach.
We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue.
We must send a strong message to countries that use terrorism as an instrument of policy and provide safe haven and support to terrorists that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.
Our shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan. India has been contributing to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to the people of Afghanistan and will continue to do so.
In today’s interconnected world, the scope of security has become even broader. The crisis in West Asia has demonstrated that a conflict in one region does not remain confined to that region. Its impact is felt across the world, affecting energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains. The countries of the Global South bear the greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on the battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy.
Drug trafficking is not merely a crime; it is a serious threat to our younger generation and regional security. The Centres being established under the SCO to address challenges such as security threats, organised crime, information security, and narcotics are a positive step. We must make these Centres an effective instrument for practical coordination and timely action.
Friends,
The second pillar of our shared development is strong and reliable connectivity. India supports all efforts that connect markets, facilitate trade, and open up new avenues for development. However, it is equally essential that such efforts respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries. This is also the fundamental spirit of the SCO Charter.
Going forward, the scope of connectivity will become even broader. Along with roads, railways, and air corridors, we must simplify customs processes, promote digital documentation, and make logistics networks more efficient.
Friends,
The third pillar is — Opportunity.
It means that the benefits of SCO cooperation should reach our people directly. Our greatest strength is the connections between our people. For India, the SCO is a confluence of great civilisations, cultures, and ideas. Over the next twenty-five years of the SCO, people-to-people ties should remain at the heart of our cooperation.
The true measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts create for young people, how many new markets open up for our entrepreneurs, how much our farmers benefit from technology, and how much better the lives of our citizens become.
This is the true meaning of “Security, Connectivity, and Opportunity.”
Our cooperation in the SCO should not be merely government-driven; it should also be people-driven. I am pleased that, under Kyrgyzstan’s chairmanship, special emphasis has been placed on youth engagement within the SCO. India has taken initiatives such as the SCO Start-up Forum, Young Authors’ Conclave, and Young Scientists’ Forum.
Last year, India proposed the SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum. I am pleased that its first session will be held in India this year. I am confident that with the active participation of all of you, this forum will become a strong platform for vibrant dialogue within the SCO.
Friends,
Kyrgyzstan’s great literary figure, Chingiz Aitmatov, gave the world a beautiful and profound thought. He said that we often focus more on the things that divide us, and less on the things that unite us.
This message is equally relevant for the SCO today. Our diversity is our identity, and our shared purpose is our strength. From Bishkek, we should move forward with this resolve:
From shared geography to shared opportunities,
from vision to outcomes,
and from government-driven cooperation to people-driven partnership.
With the same belief and commitment, India is ready to contribute to the SCO family’s shared journey.
Thank you very much.
DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister's statement. Original statement was delivered in Hindi.

content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to Shri P.A. Sangma, former Speaker, Lok Sabha, at his portrait in the Central Hall of Samvidhaan Sadan  on his birth anniversary, today.
Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh; Members of Parliament; former Members of Parliament  and other dignitaries also paid floral tributes to Shri Sangma on this occasion.
Secretary - General Lok  Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh and Secretary – General, Rajya Sabha Shri P C Mody and Officers of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha Secretariats also paid tributes to Shri Sangma.
Shri Sangma was a distinguished parliamentarian, able administrator and prominent leader from Meghalaya who made significant contributions to public life and the development of the North-Eastern region. Beginning his parliamentary career in 1977, he served as a Union Minister in various capacities and as Chief Minister of Meghalaya before being unanimously elected Speaker of the Eleventh Lok Sabha in 1996, becoming the first Member from the Opposition to hold the office. As Speaker, he was widely respected for his knowledge of parliamentary rules, commitment to the dignity and orderly conduct of the House, and efforts to strengthen parliamentary democracy. He also played an important role in promoting greater representation of women in legislatures and in strengthening inter-parliamentary relations. A nine-term Member of the Lok Sabha, Shri Sangma remained closely associated with the upliftment of the North-Eastern region, particularly tribal and disadvantaged communities, and was widely recognized for his contribution to the welfare of the working class and marginalized sections of society. Shri Sangma passed away on 4 March 2016 in New Delhi.
The portrait of Shri Sangma was painted by Shri Vijender Sharma. It is displayed in the Outer Lobby, Samvidhaan Sadan  and was unveiled by the then  President of India Shri Pranab  Mukherjee on 10th February 2014.

title: AIIA Launches ‘AyurVarta’ Digital Dialogue Series Ahead of Ayurveda Day

date:

                01 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Ayush, has launched
‘AyurVarta’
, a special digital dialogue series aimed at taking authentic knowledge, scientific perspectives and contemporary relevance of Ayurveda to wider audiences in India and abroad.
The initiative has been launched ahead of
Ayurveda Day
, which will be observed on
23 September
. The series will feature conversations with leading experts on Ayurveda, contemporary healthcare challenges, scientific research, education, clinical practice and the growing global relevance of Ayurveda.
The inaugural episode of ‘AyurVarta’ featured a discussion between
Professor (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA
, and
Professor (Dr.) Mahesh Vyas, Dean, Ph.D., AIIA
, on the theme “Why is Ayurveda Day celebrated on 23 September?”
The discussion traced the evolution of Ayurveda Day, which was earlier observed on
Dhanvantari Jayanti (Dhanteras)
, and highlighted the Government’s decision to designate
23 September as the fixed date
for its annual observance.
Speaking on the occasion,
Professor (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA
, said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, sustained efforts are being made to strengthen Ayurveda as an important knowledge and healthcare system with growing relevance in the global health landscape.
He said that the observance of Ayurveda Day on a fixed date will provide greater consistency and a stronger national and international identity to the annual celebration.
Prof. Prajapati further stated that
‘AyurVarta’
is a digital extension of this vision and will provide audiences with access to authentic knowledge and expert perspectives on Ayurveda.
During the discussion, Professor (Dr.) Mahesh Vyas,
highlighted the significance associated with 23 September, which falls around the
Autumnal Equinox
, when the duration of day and night is approximately equal.
He explained that the idea of
balance and equilibrium
is central to the Ayurvedic understanding of health and well-being. In this context, the date also provides a conceptual association with Ayurveda’s emphasis on balance, harmony and equilibrium.
‘AyurVarta’ has been conceived as a continuing digital initiative to facilitate informed dialogue on various dimensions of Ayurveda. The series will bring together Ayurveda experts, physicians, academicians, scientists, researchers and policy experts from India and abroad.
Future episodes of ‘AyurVarta’ will explore a wide range of subjects, including:
Scientific foundations of Ayurveda and contemporary research
Ayurveda education and the role of the younger generation
Ayurveda and public health
Innovation and technology in Ayurveda
Integration of Ayurveda with modern medical sciences
Medicinal plants and natural resources
Healthy lifestyles and preventive healthcare
Ayurveda and global health
International opportunities and expansion of Ayurveda
Research, evidence generation and evidence-based Ayurveda
Episodes of ‘AyurVarta’ will be disseminated through AIIA’s official digital and social media platforms, including YouTube, Facebook, X and Instagram, enabling access for students, young people, physicians, researchers, academicians and the general public.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reviews Progress of Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
subtitle:
Average score of 100 Dhan-Dhaanya districts improves from 22.54 in April to 38.85 in July 2026

Focus on outcome-based monitoring, convergence of 36 schemes and ensuring benefits reach farmers
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today reviewed the progress of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The review focused on accelerating implementation in the 100 identified districts, strengthening convergence among schemes, improving district-level performance and ensuring that interventions translate into measurable outcomes and tangible benefits for farmers.
During the review, the Minister was apprised of the progress of PM-DDKY through the scheme’s dashboard, including district-wise performance, District Action Plans, field monitoring by Central Nodal Officers (CNOs), financial progress, capacity building, convergence of schemes and mechanisms being developed to track beneficiary-level outcomes.
Data-driven monitoring of 100 districts
PM-DDKY aims to accelerate agricultural development in 100 districts identified on the basis of low agricultural productivity, low cropping intensity and low agricultural credit disbursement.
The scheme focuses on six key objectives: increasing agricultural productivity; promoting crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices; enhancing post-harvest storage capacity; improving irrigation infrastructure; enabling greater access to short- and long-term agricultural credit; and improving governance and service delivery.
The scheme is being implemented through the convergence of 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, along with State schemes and private-sector participation.
A total of 121 indicators, comprising 74 output indicators and 47 outcome indicators, have been identified across the 36 schemes for monitoring progress against annual targets. District performance on output indicators is ranked every month through the PM-DDKY dashboard, while outcome indicators will facilitate assessment of progress against the baseline.
The average score of the 100 districts across the six objectives increased from 22.54 in April 2026 to 38.85 in July 2026, an improvement of 16.31 points.
Objective-wise performance also recorded improvement during the period. The average score for agricultural productivity increased from 2.53 in April to 6.70 in July; crop diversification and sustainable agricultural practices from 5.60 to 8.65; post-harvest storage capacity from 2.61 to 3.82; irrigation infrastructure from 1.65 to 4.20; access to agricultural credit from 2.81 to 5.59; and governance and service delivery from 7.94 to 10.33.
All 100 districts have uploaded District Action Plans
The review noted that all 100 districts have uploaded their District Action Plans (DAPs) and feedback has been provided on the DAPs of all 100 districts.
All 100 districts have submitted data against output indicators up to July 2026, while all 100 districts have also submitted outcome-indicator data for the financial year 2025-26.
Committees have been constituted at the State, District and national levels for review and monitoring. Central Nodal Officers are also undertaking regular field-level monitoring of implementation.
Focus on outcomes and benefits reaching farmers
The review emphasised strengthening the monitoring framework to move beyond tracking activities and expenditure towards measuring outcomes and the actual benefits reaching farmers.
The Financial Progress Module of the PM-DDKY dashboard was implemented on 31 August 2026. A Beneficiary Progress Module is targeted for implementation by mid-September 2026 to enable systematic capture of beneficiary-level progress.
The strengthened dashboard will also facilitate consolidation of investments and interventions undertaken through Central schemes, State schemes and other sources in the Dhan-Dhaanya districts.
This will enable a comprehensive assessment of the resources deployed, activities undertaken, farmers benefited and outcomes achieved across the identified districts.
Capacity building of farmers and extension workers
Capacity development is an important component of PM-DDKY implementation. During January to July 2026, a total of 6,90,530 farmers and 88,961 extension workers were trained in various skills.
In addition, 2,20,683 farmers and extension workers were trained in natural farming during the period.
Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) are being utilised as technical partners for capacity development and field-level interventions, strengthening the agricultural extension system and facilitating dissemination of improved agricultural practices among farmers.
Strengthening convergence and partnerships
The review also focused on strengthening convergence among the 36 Central schemes of 11 Ministries and Departments, State schemes and private-sector interventions.
The Department of Public Enterprises has included adoption of PM-DDKY districts for CSR activities by Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) for 2026-27 and 2027-28, providing an additional avenue for supporting development interventions in the identified districts.
The monitoring mechanism is being strengthened to capture such convergence and investments, enabling assessment of the combined impact of interventions being implemented in the Dhan-Dhaanya districts.
PM-DDKY to complete one year in October
PM-DDKY was approved by the Union Cabinet on 16 July 2025 and officially launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 11 October 2025. The PM-DDKY dashboard was activated in the last week of October 2025, with monthly output-indicator rankings commencing from November 2025.
As the scheme approaches completion of its first year in October 2026, a programme is being planned to highlight the progress and performance of the 100 Dhan-Dhaanya districts. Progress will also be showcased during Rabi and regional conferences.
The review also considered convening a meeting of the National Executive Committee under the chairmanship of the Agriculture Minister and strengthening farmer participation through the proposed nomination of two progressive farmers in each District Dhan-Dhaanya Committee.

title: Ministry of Civil Aviation launches Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Ahmedabad
subtitle: Ahmedabad becomes the third spoke airport under India's International Aviation Hub Strategy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 8:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Civil Aviation today launched Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Ahmedabad, making it the third airport in the country to be integrated into India's Hub & Spoke framework for international passenger movement, after Varanasi and Amritsar. The launch was marked at a function attended by Union Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Ram Mohan Naidu, Gujarat Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel, Union Minister of State for Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi.
The launch of Hub & Spoke operations from Varanasi on 25 June 2026 marked the beginning of a new chapter in Indian aviation. As part of the phased expansion of the initiative, Hub & Spoke operations from Amritsar Airport were launched on 28 July 2026. Today, with the addition of Ahmedabad, we are taking another significant step towards creating an integrated, seamless and passenger-centric aviation network that connects India's regions directly with the world through our own hub airport at Delhi. Now hub-and-spoke operations from Ahmedabad will further strengthen global connectivity, with flight AI 1117 connecting passengers to 22 destinations, primarily across Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, while the evening service AI 1121, departing at 20:15 hours, will extend connectivity to 17 destinations across North America, East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and Europe.
Civil Aviation Minister Shri Ram Mohan Naidu, while explaining what changes for Ahmedabad passengers, noted that until now, a passenger travelling from Ahmedabad to destinations like Paris, Toronto or Sydney had to take a domestic flight to Delhi, manage separate bookings, handle luggage on arrival, navigate immigration queues at a large airport, and risk missing a connecting flight. Under Hub & Spoke, immigration, check-in and baggage check-through will now all be completed at Ahmedabad itself, with baggage travelling straight through to the final international destination.
The Hub-and-Spoke model is a key component of the Government's International Aviation Hub Strategy, aimed at positioning India as the preferred aviation hub for Indian travellers by 2030 and a leading global aviation hub by 2047. The initiative leverages India's strategic geographical location and extensive airport infrastructure to strengthen connectivity through Indian hubs and reduce dependence on overseas transit airports.
Under this first-of-its-kind framework, international passengers complete check-in, immigration and customs formalities at the originating spoke airport, which is itself an international airport, before commencing their journey to global destinations. After arriving at the designated hub airport, passengers can proceed directly to their onward international flight without repeating immigration or customs procedures. Baggage is transferred seamlessly, significantly improving passenger convenience and reducing travel complexity.
Talking about its potential, Shri Ram Mohan Naidu cited that 1.6 crore passengers last year travelled from Ahmedabad to Delhi to board international flights. He said that with the seamless journey of Hub & Spoke, Ahmedabad will be ready to invite a global audience from maximum destinations for the Commonwealth Games in 2030.
The Minister said the benefit of greater footfall would flow to Ahmedabad's textile, pharmaceutical, diamond and gems, and engineering sectors.
The Hub and Spoke model is expected to deliver multiple benefits, including enhanced international connectivity from Tier-II and Tier-III cities, improved passenger experience, better utilisation of airport infrastructure, greater operational efficiency for airlines, and strengthened competitiveness of Indian aviation.
The benefits extend beyond aviation. Improved international connectivity will particularly benefit Gujarat's business community, exporters including diamond exporters, handicraft artisans, investors, tourists and students, by improving access to international markets and destinations. Ahmedabad's stronger integration with the national hub network can support trade, tourism, investment and regional economic development, thereby contributing to Gujarat's growth as a globally connected state. Studies undertaken by the Ministry indicate that aviation hub development could generate approximately 0.4 million direct and indirect jobs and contribute an additional USD 30 billion to India's GDP by 2030. By 2047, the cumulative impact could support approximately 16 million direct and indirect jobs and contribute nearly USD 1.4 trillion to the economy.
The commencement of Hub and Spoke flight operations from Ahmedabad marks the extension of this progressively expanding framework to additional airports across the country in the coming months. Shri Ram Mohan Naidu shared that Hub & Spoke connectivity will next be extended to 22 more airports in this phase, including Surat in Gujarat.
Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Shri Manoj Kumar Das, Chief Secretary, Govt. of Gujarat; Shri Rajesh Nirwan, DG, DGCA; Shri Puneet Kansal, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; and representatives from the Bureau of Immigration, Customs and CISF were also present. The occasion also witnessed the presence of a wide spectrum of industry associations, hotel and hospitality stakeholders, travel partners, tourism representatives and other key aviation and trade stakeholders, reflecting the strong collaborative support for strengthening international connectivity from Ahmedabad.

title: Advisor to Prime Minister, Shri Tarun Kapoor Reviews Rehabilitation and Development Initiatives at Belgaria and Karmatand Townships

During his visit, Shri Kapoor reviewed various initiatives being implemented for families affected by the Jharia mine fires and interacted with rehabilitated families and local residents to understand their requirements, expectations and concerns.
The visit formed part of a comprehensive review of BCCL’s operational activities, modern mining technologies, Jharia fire management and rehabilitation and development initiatives under the Jharia Master Plan.
Education and Skill Development Initiatives at Karmatand
Shri Kapoor began the day two with a visit to Karmatand Township, where he inspected the Middle/High School and interacted with students to take stock of the educational environment and basic facilities available at the institution. He also planted a sapling on the school premises, reinforcing the importance of environmental conservation.
Shri Kapoor thereafter visited BCCL’s Multi Skill Development Institute (MSDI-IV), where he interacted with youth undergoing training in trades including Beautician, Customer Care Executive and Assistant Fitter. The MSDI-IV centre is being operated in collaboration with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) with the objective of enhancing employability and creating employment opportunities for youth from rehabilitated families.
Around 800 youth have successfully completed training at the centres so far, while more than 250 trainees are currently undergoing training in various trades. The training programmes range from two-and-a-half to three months, with a majority of trained candidates having secured employment or placement with different companies.
The initiative reflects BCCL’s continued focus on linking rehabilitation with sustainable livelihood opportunities and enabling rehabilitated families, particularly their youth, to benefit from skill development and employment opportunities.
Review of Rehabilitation and Livelihood Initiatives at Belgaria
The high-level delegation subsequently visited Belgaria Township and reviewed various rehabilitation and development initiatives. Shri Kapoor interacted with local residents and sought their feedback on the facilities available in the township as well as their requirements for further development. Residents highlighted the need for expansion of existing facilities and upgradation of older housing units.
Shri Kapoor emphasised that the objective of the rehabilitation programme is not merely relocation but to ensure that families affected by mine fires are provided with safe, dignified and improved living conditions. He stressed the importance of strengthening education, healthcare, skill development, employment, livelihood opportunities and other basic amenities through coordinated efforts of all concerned agencies.
Joint Secretary, Ministry of Textiles Smt. Alaknanda Dayal, highlighted the potential for creating local employment and livelihood opportunities in the rehabilitation areas, including through the textile sector. She particularly underlined the emerging opportunities in handmade fibre and technical textiles and provided necessary guidance to the concerned officials.
Promoting Local Livelihoods and Community Development
As part of the visit, Shri Kapoor also inspected stalls established by Self-Help Groups (SHGs) under JharShilp and Project Aarohi with the support of BCCL’s CSR & JMP initiatives. The stalls showcased handicraft items and a range of artisanal products, reflecting the skills and entrepreneurial potential of local communities and the scope for strengthening sustainable livelihood opportunities through community-based initiatives.
During the visit to Jharia Vihar Colony, Shri Kapoor inaugurated an upgraded Primary School, a Health Sub Centre and a Model Anganwadi Centre-cum-Pre-Nursery School. He also visited RSP College, in Phase-I and reviewed the proposed infrastructure upgradation and other developmental activities planned for the institution.
Skill Development and Textile Production at Belgaria
Shri Kapoor further inspected BCCL’s MSDI-II, where training is currently being imparted in various trades, including multi skill technician. He also reviewed the activities of the Skill Development and Production Centre, being developed through the collaborative efforts of BCCL, the Jharia Rehabilitation and Development Authority (JRDA),
Jharkhand Govt. and Rajdhani Universal Fabrics Private Limited.
The centre has been established with the objective of promoting skill development, employment and sustainable livelihood opportunities for local communities. Following completion of the ongoing training programmes, Rajdhani Textiles in the initial phase shall commence skill training and production activities related to the textile industry at the centre. The initiative is expected to strengthen the linkage between skill development, local employment and production-oriented livelihood opportunities.
High-Level Review Meeting at Dhanbad
The visit concluded with a high-level review meeting chaired by Shri Tarun Kapoor at the Dhanbad Collectorate. The meeting reviewed the progress of rehabilitation, infrastructure and developmental activities being undertaken by JRDA and other concerned departments under the Jharia Master Plan.
Shri Kapoor directed the concerned agencies to accelerate rehabilitation efforts and accord priority to the safe and dignified rehabilitation of affected families. He also emphasised the need to further strengthen education, healthcare, livelihood generation, skill development and basic infrastructure in the rehabilitation areas. He stressed the importance of close coordination among all implementing agencies and called for timely and result-oriented execution of ongoing and planned initiatives.
The meeting and field visits were attended by Coal India Chairman Shri B. Sairam; CMD BCCL, Shri Manoj Kumar Agarwal; Joint Secretary (Ministry of Textiles) Smt. Alaknanda Dayal; Project Advisor, (MoC), Shri Alok Kumar Singh and other senior officials from the Ministry of Coal, district administration, JRDA, BCCL and other concerned departments.
The two-day visit provided an opportunity for a comprehensive review of BCCL’s operational activities, modern mining technologies, Jharia fire management and rehabilitation and development initiatives under the Jharia Master Plan.

In continuation with the initiatives taken by the Government from time to time to promote Ease of Doing Business for the exporting community, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has enabled automated issuance of Free Sale and Commerce Certificates (FSC) on the DGFT portal. These Certificates are issued to exporters, under Foreign Trade Policy, for items which are not covered under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940. At present, such certificates are issued by Regional Authorities (RAs) of DGFT after scrutiny and verification.
Eligible applications will now be considered for automatic issuance in accordance with the prevailing framework, without being routed for manual scrutiny. The automated mechanism is expected to reduce processing time for a significant category of FSC applications and lower the compliance burden associated with the earlier manual process.
Applications requiring verification, or those not meeting the automated processing parameters, may continue to be routed to the concerned RA for manual processing.
Certain auto-approved applications may also be subsequently flagged to the concerned RA for review under the system's risk management parameters.
The measure is expected to reduce avoidable manual intervention, improve the predictability of processing and facilitate faster issuance of FSCs for eligible exporters, while retaining appropriate verification and oversight for applications requiring scrutiny. By strengthening automated, rule-based processing and applying risk-based review, the initiative is expected to make the issuance of Free Sale and Commerce Certificates more efficient, transparent and predictable for exporters and administering authorities.

Together, these new platforms represent an important expansion of IPPB’s proposition from enabling everyday banking and payments to creating greater access to protection, investment and financial security.

To take the financial inclusion journey forward, IPPB rolled out three product variants during the last year:

IPPB was launched on September 1, 2018. The Bank has been set up with the vision to build the most accessible, affordable and trusted bank for the common man in India. title: States/UTs Food Secretaries Conference reviews various issues pertaining to Department of Food and Public Distribution
subtitle:
New Storage Policy envisages 131 LMT additional storage capacity

States advised to complete Vehicle Location Tracking System (VLTS) implementation by December 2026

e-KYC coverage reaches 90.64% as on 30 July 2026
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 8:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Secretary, Department of Food & Public Distribution (DFPD), Government of India, Shri Sanjeev Chopra chaired a meeting of State Food Secretaries on 1 September 2026 in New Delhi to review key issues relating to procurement, public distribution and storage of foodgrains. Food Secretaries of various States/UTs and officers of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) attended the meeting.
Paddy Procurement and Improved Rice
Following deliberations with States/UTs, the paddy procurement estimates for the ensuing Kharif Marketing Season (KMS) 2026–27 was fixed at 708.64 LMT in terms of paddy.
The implementation of
Improved Rice under PMGKAY
and other welfare schemes was also reviewed. Under the approved policy, raw rice procured will contain up to 10% broken grains, replacing the existing specification of 25%. For parboiled rice, the limit will be 5% broken grains, replacing the existing specification of 16%.
Procurement of Improved Rice will commence from KMS 2026–27 and will be progressively expanded across procuring States. States were requested to assess milling capacity, plan necessary upgradation and prepare a phased roadmap for implementation.
A quantity of 18.85 LMT of coarse grains has been estimated for procurement by States during KMS 2026–27 (Kharif).
Coarse Grains, Millets and Procurement Technology
The procurement and distribution plans for coarse grains, millets and minor millets were reviewed. The Conference was informed that 16.38 LMT of coarse grains and millets were procured during 2025–26, the highest procurement recorded during the last five years.
Progress under the
Procurement Centre Smart-Assessment Portal (PCSAP)
was reviewed, including the introduction of AI-based image validation from KMS 2026–27.
The Conference also reviewed the progress of Joint Physical Verification (JPV). The proposed online physical verification of paddy at the end of the procurement season, starting from KMS 2026–27, was discussed with the States.
Successful initiatives and best practices of States were also recognised:
Andhra Pradesh – Best Implementation of the Improved Rice Scheme
Punjab – Best Performance in JPV and PCSAP
Karnataka – Excellence in Procurement of Shree Anna
Chhattisgarh – First State to implement AgriStack in paddy procurement
Storage Capacity and Depot Darpan
The Conference reviewed the
New Storage Policy
, which seeks to address the growing mismatch between procurement and offtake, regional imbalances and under-utilisation of storage capacity.
The Policy envisages creation of 131 LMT additional storage capacity, including 111 LMT by States and 20 LMT by FCI. Identified States were requested to submit time-bound action plans.
States were also advised to onboard their foodgrain storage facilities on the Depot Darpan Portal, a self-assessment tool for warehouses, undertake assessments within defined timelines and avail training and handholding support from CWC, FCI and DFPD.
Technology-enabled Foodgrain Movement
The implementation of the
Vehicle Location Tracking System (VLTS)
for GPS-based real-time tracking of vehicles transporting foodgrains under the PDS supply chain was reviewed.
States were advised to complete implementation by December 2026, with identified States targeted for completion by September 2026.
The
Procurement Optimisation Tool
, supporting both KMS and RMS, was also reviewed. The tool has been security-audited and installed in Punjab and Haryana. Remaining States were requested to prepare and update Procurement Centre, Mill and Warehouse data in the system by 15 September 2026.
The Conference further reviewed the integration of Anna Chakra with State SCMS and VLTS to eliminate manual intervention in data exchange. Integration has been completed for six States. Remaining States were advised to complete integration in a phased manner by September and December 2026 and ensure verification and updation of FPS, warehouse and commodity master data.
PDS Reforms and Technology-enabled Services
The Conference reviewed key initiatives relating to PDS reforms and technology-enabled service delivery, including onboarding and the way forward under
SMART-PDS, SARTHAK-PDS, e-KYC and mobile number seeding, as well as the Mera Ration and Anna Mitra
mobile applications.
Discussions also covered rationalisation of Fair Price Shops, CBDC, identification of silent and duplicate beneficiaries, grievance redressal, intra-State movement and FPS dealer margins, and strengthening of vigilance mechanisms.
Digital Rupee-based DBT for FPS Dealer Margins
The Digital Rupee (₹)-based Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) pilot for FPS dealer margins, already inaugurated in Gujarat, Puducherry, and Chandigarh & Dadra Nagar Haveli, will be extended to the entire Delhi State and two districts each in six more States — Andhra Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu.
A review workshop is scheduled at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, on 11 September 2026.
SARTHAK-PDS and Fair Price Shops
SARTHAK-PDS, the umbrella scheme for 2026–31 integrating assistance to States for intra-State movement of foodgrains and FPS dealer margins with the SMART-PDS technology layer, has seen 100% of Mother Sanction issued to States/UTs for FY 2026–27.
e-KYC and Ration Card Data
e-KYC stood at 90.64% as of 30 July 2026. A new Standard Operating Procedure
(SOP) for e-KYC-based data replication and mobile-number seeding
through ePOS was rolled out. The Department reiterated that this will facilitate easier delivery of foodgrains to beneficiaries.
New SOPs for silent ration cards and duplicate beneficiaries, issued under the amended TPDS (Control) Order, 2015, provide for temporary disablement followed by a three-month e-KYC revalidation window. The functionality will go live in SMART-PDS from 1 October 2026.
Strengthening Vigilance Mechanisms
States/UTs were advised to ensure timely constitution and regular functioning of Vigilance Committees and submit prescribed status reports in accordance with Section 29 of the NFSA, 2013.
States/UTs were also directed to operationalise Aadhaar-based authentication of foodgrain receipt at the Fair Price Shop level by Vigilance Committees and submit rollout compliance reports within four weeks.

title: Government reduces sugar stock holding limit for sugar dealers to 2,000 quintals from 15th September
subtitle: New stock limit aimed to curb hoarding and speculative trading, protect consumer interest by ensuring adequate availability and price stability
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 1:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Government of India has reduced the stock holding limit for sugar dealers from
4,000 quintals to 2,000 quintals
, effective from
15th September, 2026 till 30th November, 2026
, to ensure adequate availability of sugar in the domestic market and to prevent hoarding and speculative trading of sugar. At present, a stock holding limit of
4,000 quintals
on sugar dealers across the country is effective from
1st August, 2026
. The Government has now taken further measures by reducing the stock holding limit to
2,000 quintals
.
Under the amended provisions, with effect from
15th September, 2026
, a sugar dealer shall:
Not hold any stock for a period exceeding 30 days
from the date of receipt of such stock.
Not keep sugar in stock, at any time and in any place throughout the country, in excess of 2,000 quintals.
However, considering the specific market requirements of the region, the
stock holding limit shall remain
at
4,000 quintals for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas
.
The Kolkata area is sourcing sugar from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra and supplying to the eastern part of the country, including the North-Eastern region. Therefore, the existing limit of 4,000 quintals has been retained for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas.
The measure is aimed at
further curbing hoarding, discouraging speculative trading and preventing excessive accumulation of sugar stocks
. It will facilitate the orderly movement of sugar through the supply chain and ensure its continuous availability to consumers at reasonable prices.
Intensive monitoring and physical verification
The Government has undertaken
intensive monitoring and physical verification of sugar stocks across the country
, covering sugar mills, dealers and traders. The exercise has helped identify instances of
excess holding, non-disclosure and irregularities in the movement and sale of sugar stocks
.
As a result of these interventions and improved market availability,
ex-mill sugar prices have declined by around 20% in recent days
. Retail prices have also started showing a downward trend and are expected to follow the reduction in ex-mill prices.
Regular stock declaration and continued monitoring
The Government has been closely monitoring developments in the sugar market and has also put in place a mechanism for
regular declaration and updating of sugar stocks through the Department of Food & Public Distribution’s online portal
. Physical verification of sugar stocks across the country, covering sugar mills, dealers and traders, shall continue in the coming weeks. The Government assures consumers that it is taking all necessary steps to maintain
adequate availability, orderly supplies and price stability of sugar in the domestic market
, while ensuring that genuine trade and distribution activities continue without disruption.

Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs, under Ministry of Corporate Affairs hosted two senior bureaucrats resource persons, who delivered lectures under the aegis of “Weekend Wisdom Programme” recently. Welcoming the first guest, Sh. Anindo Majumdar an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) of the 1985 batch and have nearly four decades of rich and varied experience in different areas of public administration, Sh. Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, DG &CEO, IICA mentioned that as Secretary Chief Vigilance Commission and in current posting as Member (Administrative) of the Central Administrative Tribunal, Kolkata his contribution towards fostering ethical behavior in public life is greatly admired. He further added efficacy of soft power in hostile terrain of Afghanistan as Development Advisor in the National Institution Building Project, paved the way for people’s involvement in the development process.
In his interaction with PGIP/LLM students, on the subject ‘Ethics and Corporate Governance’, Sh. Anindo Majumdar highlighted finer distinction between law and ethics. Drawing example from apartheid regime in South Africa, he elaborated that the regime had the backing of law, yet it was blatantly unethical.
With decades of experience at the very heart of India's vigilance and administrative machinery, Shri Majumdar brought to the students not just theory but wisdom of his experience backed by real stories of integrity, accountability, and encouraged students to uphold ethics in public life by simple message that “one should never say yes when apparent answer from the conscience is no’.
He enriched the discussion by dwelling diverse philosophies that explain ethics in a governance system, have conversations on whistle-blowers, and "regulatory capture", and the need for and importance of ethical leadership in corporate structures.
Second power talk of the day was delivered by Dr Rajajendra Kumar, IAS, Secretary Border Road Organization, Ministry of Home Affairs on the topics, “Corporate Governance, Cyber Security, Personal Data Protection and Artificial Intelligence” and “Smart Border Management”.  Welcoming the guest of honour, Sh. Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh DG &CEO, IICA mentioned that Dr. Kumar conceptualized and implemented the Mobile Seva project, which won the UN Public Service Award in 2014. This project enabled government services to be delivered via mobile devices, significantly expanding digital access for citizens. His work has had a lasting impact on making government services more accessible, secure, and efficient for millions of Indians.
Delving with Core philosophy behind Artificial Intelligence, BRO’s Dr Rajendra Kumar highlighted that underlying message is continuous innovation, inclusivity, responsible deployment and govern with trust.  Pillar I of AI policy focuses on Promotion AI-led research in continuum, entrepreneurship, productivity and institutional transformation through collaboration among government, academia and industry. Pillar II is important to bridge the void between haves and have not. Inclusive development is the key. Pillar III addresses responsibility, with a view to ensure AI is ethical, safe, transparent, fair and human-centric, with safeguards for privacy, bias, security and accountability and pillar IV aims at addressing governance issues with development of proportionate and adaptive regulatory framework with clear accountability, standards, monitoring, auditability and grievance redressal.
He added that the New Corporate Trust Equation rests on four interconnected pillars: Good Governance creates accountability, Cybersecurity builds resilience, Personal Data Protection strengthens trust, and Responsible AI enables sustainable innovation. Together, these pillars provide the foundation for a modern corporate ecosystem in which organisations are not only efficient and innovative, but also transparent, secure, ethical and accountable; thereby creating enduring trust among stakeholders and supporting sustainable long-term value creation.
In his talk on Smart Border management, Dr Rajendra Kumar added that technology should also strengthen border infrastructure delivery and quality control. Extensive use of GIS mapping, Drone inspection, and digital dashboards add administrative value by way of facilitating quicker review, sharper accountability and better utilization of funds and manpower.

title: Invest in R&D and technology upgradation while fostering partnerships to become global enterprises & achieve Viksit Bharat goal: Raksha Mantri to MSMEs
subtitle: “Our manufacturing vision must be guided by the principle of ‘Make in India, Make for India, and Make for the World’”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon MSMEs to invest a portion of their turnover in Research, Development and Technology Upgradation while fostering partnerships with universities, IITs, research institutions, DRDO labs, start-ups, and large industries to evolve from mere domestic suppliers to global enterprises and achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat@2047. Addressing an MSME event in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh on September 01, 2026, he asserted that Viksit Bharat signifies a nation that is globally competitive in manufacturing, a leader in technology and innovation, and self-reliant in its strategic and economic capabilities, capable of generating ample employment opportunities for the youth.
Emphasising on strengthening the global competitiveness of Indian MSMEs, Raksha Mantri stated that the ongoing transformation of global supply chains and the growing demand for reliable manufacturing partners present a significant opportunity for India. He highlighted the steps being taken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to deepen India’s trade partnerships with key nations, including through Free Trade Agreements with the US, UK, New Zealand, Oman, Switzerland and the European Union. “These FTA networks open up a vast ocean of opportunities for global trade and exports for MSMEs and industries. They must fully leverage these international partnerships and trade agreements through government schemes such as Credit Guarantee Expansion and GST Rationalization, and take Indian products to every corner of the globe. Our manufacturing vision must be guided by the principle of ‘Make in India, Make for India, and Make for the World’,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh enumerated the Government’s efforts towards integrating MSMEs into the formal economy and creating an enabling ecosystem for their growth, pointing out that the number of MSMEs has increased from around 4.67 crore in 2012-13 to approximately 08 crore today. This reflects the growing depth and dynamism of India’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, he said.
Highlighting the immense potential of MSMEs in defence manufacturing, Raksha Mantri said initiatives such as Innovations for DeiDEX) and Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX (ADITI) are enabling start-ups, innovators and MSMEs to develop cutting-edge solutions for the Defence Forces. He urged MSME entrepreneurs to view the sector as a gateway to technology, innovation and global business opportunities. He identified drones, Artificial Intelligence, robotics, cybersecurity, advanced electronics, sensors, autonomous systems, advanced materials, space and quantum technologies as areas offering immense opportunities for Indian MSMEs.
Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that technology alone cannot drive growth and global competitiveness of MSMEs as equal attention must be given to quality, skill development, technology upgradation, market access and finance. “Indian MSMEs must establish their identity in global markets through quality and reliability. The importance of these attributes is even greater in the defence sector, where the reliability of every component directly affects the operational effectiveness of the Defence Forces. The defence manufacturing ecosystem must remain committed to the principle of ‘Zero Defect’ and ‘Zero Compromise on Quality’,” he said. He underlined the need to equip the youth with industry-relevant skills and encourage MSMEs to continuously upskill their workforce to meet the demands of modern industry.
Raksha Mantri further called for making advanced technologies such as digital manufacturing, automation, Artificial Intelligence and modern production methods more accessible and affordable for MSMEs. He highlighted market access as a key enabler of scale, urging greater participation of MSMEs in government procurement, the vendor ecosystems of large industries and export markets. Emphasising finance as perhaps the most critical requirement for MSME growth, he said that timely and affordable access to capital must go hand in hand with financial discipline and sound business practices. These five pillars, he said, will be essential for enabling India’s MSMEs to become globally competitive and contribute meaningfully to the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the special significance of North India’s MSME sector in India’s industrial development, noting its strong presence across manufacturing, engineering, automobiles, electronics, defence, textiles, food processing and services. He said that the Defence Industrial Corridor, particularly in Uttar Pradesh, has created new opportunities for defence manufacturing, with the state emerging not merely as a large market but as an important hub of India’s new manufacturing and defence ecosystem. He urged MSMEs in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Delhi and Haryana to fully leverage these opportunities and evolve from being suppliers to large defence companies into technology developers, system suppliers and exporters.
Raksha Mantri called for inspiring the country’s youth to become job creators rather than job seekers, underlining that entrepreneurship is an important instrument of nation-building. He stressed the need to create greater opportunities for women & youth and develop small cities and towns as new centres of economic growth. “The vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 is not merely a government objective but a collective aspiration, requiring joint efforts of government, industry, MSMEs, start-ups, academia and civil society. The progress of an MSME is the progress of India,” he said.

During the meeting, Raksha Mantri, along with Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, was briefed by Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar and the Chairmen & Managing Directors (CMDs) of the DPSUs on their performance, key achievements, and future roadmap. Raksha Mantri reviewed the progress made by the DPSUs in enhancing indigenous production and manufacturing capabilities, development of advanced defence technologies, increasing defence exports, strengthening supply chains and execution of major projects.
In his address, Raksha Mantri commended the DPSUs for their steadfast contribution to strengthening India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem and advancing the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat while building a robust defence industrial base ecosystem. He stated that all the 16 DPSUs are showing their achievement in multi sectors and congratulated the organizations for their continued dedication and excellence. He underlined that in the year 2025-26, India achieved defence production worth approx. Rs 1.8 lakh crore with DPSUs contributing Rs. 1.29 lakh crore. He termed the achievement a reflection of the nation’s significant progress towards building an Aatmanirbhar defence industrial base.
Shri Rajnath Singh urged the DPSUs to focus on timely delivery, reducing the import dependency, transforming R&D into technology leadership, enhancing defence exports to newer heights, increasing productivity with their capex expansion, supporting start-ups & MSMEs further and making efforts to achieve quality equivalent to global standards. “The progress of DPSUs is not merely an economic or industrial necessity; it is a national security imperative. Recent global conflicts have demonstrated how crucial assured supply chains, surge capacity, critical spares, rapid repair capabilities, and the ability to sustain production during prolonged conflicts are for any nation,” he said.
While Raksha Mantri welcomed the increased investment in R&D by DPSUs, he stated that the success of R&D should be measured not just by the amount spent, but by the development of new technologies, intellectual property, prototypes, and operational products. “We must identify niche technology areas where India can become not just self-reliant, but a global leader,” he said.
Raksha Mantri urged the DPSUs to continue focusing on elevating the quality of their products to global standards. “In pursuit of the ‘Make in India, Make for the World’ objective, we must resolve to transform all DPSUs into global giants,” he said.
During the event, the CMDs of seven DPSUs - Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), BEML, and MIDHANI - presented dividend cheques, worth a total of Rs 3,951 crore for the Government's equity shares to the Raksha Mantri for FY 2025-26.

The ‘National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme’, implemented by the Department of School Education & Literacy, Union Ministry of Education, awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level, i.e., Class VIII and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level, i.e., Class XII.
The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class IX students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State/UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes X to XII based on the student's academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools. The scholarship amount is Rs. 12,000 per annum per student.
NMMSS scholarships are disbursed directly into the bank accounts of selected students by electronic transfer through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) following DBT mode. The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than Rs. 3.50 lakh per annum, a minimum of 55% marks or equivalent grade in the Class VII examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship (relaxable by 5% for SC/ST students).
The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) - the one-stop platform for scholarship schemes disbursed to students by the Government of India. As of 31.08.2026, 79,398 fresh and 1,87, 208 renewal applications have been submitted.
All eligible students are advised to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) within the extended timeline. Students who have already submitted their applications should also ensure that their applications are duly verified by the concerned Institute/District/State Nodal Officers, as applicable.
On the NSP portal, there are two levels of verification of the scholarship application of selected students, Level-1 (L1) verification is at the Institute Nodal Officer (INO) and Level-2 (L2) is with the District Nodal Officer (DNO). The last date for INO level (L1) verification is 15.10.2026 and for DNO level (L2) verification is 31.10.2026.

title: Digital India BHASHINI Division Organises BHASHINI SANGAM Workshop in Nepal; Strengthens India–Nepal Collaboration on Multilingual AI

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the Embassy of India, Kathmandu, and Kathmandu University, organised BHASHINI SANGAM: INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENT WORKSHOP (NEPAL) in Kathmandu. The workshop brought together stakeholders from government, academia, technology, research and innovation ecosystems to explore the potential of multilingual and voice-first Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enabling access to digital services, information and opportunities in preferred languages.
The workshop marked an important step in strengthening India–Nepal collaboration in Language AI, building on the Memorandum of Understanding between DIBD and Kathmandu University for collaboration on language technology and digital public infrastructure. The engagement focused on taking this partnership forward through the co-creation of technology, datasets and locally relevant applications that respond to the linguistic needs of communities across both countries.
BHASHINI SANGAM is an international engagement initiative of the Digital India BHASHINI Division that brings together governments, academia, researchers, developers, startups, language experts and communities to explore the potential of Language AI beyond linguistic and geographical boundaries. The initiative focuses on co-creating Language AI with countries and communities, bringing together technology and local knowledge to build solutions rooted in their linguistic and cultural contexts. It also seeks to preserve languages and cultures in the digital age, ensuring that the voices, knowledge and identities carried by languages are represented in the technologies of tomorrow. Through such engagements, BHASHINI SANGAM aims to turn shared linguistic and cultural connections into shared innovation, co-creation and stronger partnerships, advancing a more inclusive multilingual AI ecosystem across borders.
The BHASHINI team conducted live demonstrations of its multilingual AI capabilities, showcasing speech recognition, real-time translation, voice-enabled interaction and document processing, while highlighting how Language AI can make digital access more natural and inclusive.
A dedicated BhashaDaan session highlighted the role of language data and community participation in building representative AI, with participants exploring contributions across speech, text and image.
The workshop also explored local applications in Nepali and other languages, bringing together BHASHINI’s technology ecosystem and Kathmandu University’s academic and research capabilities to develop solutions relevant to communities in India and Nepal.
Shri Suman Shekhar, First Secretary, Embassy of India, Kathmandu, said, “The MoU between DIBD and Kathmandu University provides a strong foundation for taking this collaboration forward. Together, we have an opportunity to develop local applications in Nepali, Maithili and other languages that can create meaningful value for people across India and Nepal.”
Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, said, “India and Nepal share languages, communities and a deep cultural connection, creating a unique opportunity to build Language AI together. Our aim is not just to make technology understand Nepali, Newari and Maithili, but to build with these languages, their communities and the people who speak them.”
The workshop brought together researchers, students, language experts, developers, startups and ecosystem partners to exchange ideas and explore collaboration around language datasets, research and real-world Language AI solutions.
Bhashini Sangam: International Engagement Workshop (Nepal) marks a step towards a shared India–Nepal Language AI ecosystem, bringing technology, academia, government and communities together to make language a bridge to digital inclusion.
About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India’s national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, powers 800+ government websites, has enabled 9 billion+ cumulative AI inferences, and processes 24 million+ AI inferences daily, helping make Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI.

title: Shri Bhupender Yadav calls on 4th Indo-German Environment Forum to Strengthen Knowledge, Scale Solutions and Build Stronger Institutional Capacity in Environmental Conservation

India a Role Model in Renewable Energy Expansion; Germany keen to deepen Strategic Partnership: German Environment Minister H.E. Carsten Schneider

India, Germany sign Joint Declaration of Intent on Conservation and Wise Use of Wetlands of International Importance
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

                01 SEP 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today said that environmental challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution and resource depletion require integrated and collaborative solutions. Addressing the opening session of the 4th Indo-German Environment Forum (IGEF), Shri Yadav said that the theme -
Together For More Resilience
- reflects the need for stronger cooperation to build climate-resilient, resource-efficient and sustainable development pathways. The Minister co-chaired the event along with German Minister for Environment, Climate Protection, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety, H.E. Carsten Schneider, in New Delhi today.
The IGEF is the highest-level bilateral forum between India and Germany on environmental policy and has been held since 2008. It was jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, and the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Protection, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN), Germany, in association with the Asia-Pacific Committee of German Business (APA) and the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).
Addressing the Forum, Shri Yadav noted that environmental sustainability can no longer be addressed in isolation, and emphasised the need for cooperation in building a climate-resilient future. The Minister said that India’s development experience has demonstrated that environmental ambition and economic development need not be competing objectives. He said India has been consistently achieving its commitments under its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) ahead of schedule, reflecting the scale at which environmental transformation is taking place in the country.
Highlighting the economic potential of resource efficiency and circularity, the Minister said India’s circular economy has the potential to generate a market value of more than USD 2 trillion and create close to 10 million jobs by 2050. He said the establishment of the Resource Efficiency and Circular Economy Industry Coalition during India’s G20 Presidency was an important step in bringing resource efficiency and circularity into the global economic conversation.
The Minister also highlighted that the next phase of industry transition must address the complex challenge of decarbonising energy-intensive sectors such as steel, cement and chemicals. He stressed that this transition would require innovation, cleaner energy, resource efficiency, appropriate policy frameworks and new production processes. Shri Yadav called for the Indo-German Environment Forum to focus on strengthening the knowledge and evidence base for environmental decision-making, advancing practical and scalable approaches for climate, biodiversity and resource efficiency, and building stronger institutional capacities for implementation. He added that international cooperation on knowledge, technology and innovation would be crucial in advancing this transition.
Addressing the event, H.E. Carsten Schneider said India’s rapid expansion of renewable energy, with solar panels and wind turbines coming up across the country, makes it a role model for other regions of the world. He said India was truly a country of the future, marked by a strong sense of momentum and progress and an inspiring innovative spirit among its young population.
The German Minister noted that  foundations of India-Germany relations were solid, with the two countries celebrating 75 years of diplomatic relations this year. He said India and Germany shared the common goal of ensuring that sustainable development goes hand in hand with economic growth. Welcoming the decision to expand cooperation on climate adaptation and wetland protection, he said the two countries would develop joint projects and share knowledge and experience.
On the sidelines of the Forum, Shri Yadav and H.E. Schneider held a bilateral meeting and reaffirmed the commitment on advancing environment sustainability and climate action. The ministers also signed a Joint Declaration of Intent (JDI) on Conservation and Wise Use of Wetlands of International Importance. Shri Yadav said that the JDI would provide a platform for strengthening scientific understanding, sharing good practices in wetland management, developing restoration approaches and enhancing community participation.
Earlier during the event, Shri Yadav addressed the Indo-German Business Forum on the sidelines of the event. He spoke about the immense potential for collaboration in the green transition, particularly in renewable energy, energy storage, green hydrogen, energy efficiency, sustainable manufacturing and associated technologies. The Indo-German partnership has a strong foundation, and both countries are working closely to strengthen economic resilience while simultaneously advancing the transition towards low-carbon, resource-efficient and climate-resilient economies, he noted.
The Forum provided a platform for bilateral exchanges among policymakers, private-sector representatives, think tanks and other key stakeholders on environmental and climate cooperation between the two countries. Representatives from ministries, businesses, expert groups and non-governmental organisations participated in the Forum. Through thematic sessions, the Forum focused on challenges, solutions and opportunities in the areas of Low-Carbon Industries; Biodiversity in Wetlands, Mountains and Forests; Resource Efficiency & Circular Economy as a Business Model; and Sustainable Finance, Green Skills & Investment Mobilization.
Ahead of the Forum, the three Joint Working Groups on Climate Change, Biodiversity and Circular Economy met this year. The respective working groups discussed the progress made and areas of mutual interest. The Forum assumes significance in the context of the strong and growing economic and industrial linkages between India and Germany and the potential for deeper cooperation in sustainable technologies and green economy.

Letter of Authorization for high-sea fishing from ₹25,000 to ₹5,000

.

Highlighting the vast potential of marine fisheries, inland fisheries and seaweed cultivation in Puducherry, he stated that initiatives under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) are transforming the sector into a modern economic activity while creating new livelihood opportunities for fishers. He also lauded the role of fisherwomen in successfully adopting seaweed cultivation and reiterated the Government's commitment to expanding the sector through technology-driven interventions and capacity building.
Shri K. Kailashnathan, Hon’ble Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry
, highlighted the pivotal role of the fisheries sector in India's economic growth, food security and employment generation, and underscored the Government of India's strong commitment to the welfare of fishing communities under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister. He noted that fisheries projects worth ₹350.26 crore have been implemented in Puducherry between 2021 and 2024-25, including ₹296.43 crore as Central assistance. He further informed that projects worth ₹349.14 crore have been planned in Puducherry under PMMSY over the next five years. Highlighting key initiatives launched during the event and stated that it would enhance fisheries infrastructure, generate employment, increase fishers' incomes and transform Puducherry into a modern hub of the Blue Economy. He also emphasized the potential of seaweed farming in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for fisherwomen and strengthening the coastal economy.
Shri N. Rangasamy,
Hon’ble Chief Minister of Puducherry,
highlighted that the Government of India, under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister, has been implementing several initiatives to enhance fisheries production, increase exports and improve the livelihoods of fisherfolk. He noted that nearly ₹130 crore has been allocated for the fisheries sector and emphasized the benefits being extended to fishers through diesel subsidy, boat subsidy, fishing ban period assistance, old-age support and educational assistance. He further announced that the Government would provide full financial support for the education of children from fishing families, from school to higher education. Underscoring the importance of the fisheries sector in strengthening the economy and ensuring nutritional security, he urged fishers to make optimum use of the infrastructure being created under various schemes, including PMMSY, and stressed the need for its proper maintenance to secure long-term benefits for the fishing community.
Puducherry is emerging as a model for sustainable and infrastructure-led fisheries development under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). Blessed with rich marine resources and a vibrant fishing community, the Union Territory has witnessed significant investments in modern fisheries infrastructure, including the upgradation of the Thengaithittu Fishing Harbour and the establishment of a state-of-the-art Fish Landing Centre at Nallavadu. These facilities have enhanced fish handling, berthing, auctioning and safety arrangements, benefiting thousands of fishers and over 600 fishing families in the coastal region.
Further strengthening fisheries sector, the Government of India has adopted a cluster-based approach under PMMSY by notifying
Karaikal as a Fishing Harbour Cluster
and undertaking the development of a
Smart and Integrated Fishing Harbour at Karaikal
with an investment of
₹119.94 crore
. The project will provide modern infrastructure for safe vessel berthing, hygienic fish handling and efficient fish marketing, while improving operational efficiency across the fisheries value chain. The integrated cluster approach will also promote the growth of
Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs)
and fisheries cooperatives through enhanced access to infrastructure, finance, technology, value addition and markets, enabling collective participation across the value chain, unlocking Puducherry's untapped fisheries potential, increasing fishers' incomes and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for coastal communities.

title: The Role of IIS Officers Goes Beyond Communication: They Are a Vital Link Between Governance and Citizens’ Aspirations, Building Trust through Accuracy, Credibility and Compassion: I&B Secretary
subtitle:

date:

                01 SEP 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC) today hosted the Valedictory Function and Graduation Ceremony for Group A Officer Trainees of the Indian Information Service (IIS), representing the 2009, 2023 and 2024 batches.
The ceremony marked a historic milestone for IIMC and the Indian Information Service, with IIMC conferring postgraduate degrees on IIS Officer Trainees for the first time after becoming a Deemed to be University.
The Officer Trainees were awarded the MA in Public Communication & Governance on successful completion of the prescribed academic and professional requirements. The introduction of the MA programme represents an important step towards further strengthening the academic component of IIS professional training and integrating the study of public communication, media and governance.
At the valedictory function, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said that public communication is an integral part of governance and must evolve with changing technologies and platforms. He noted that officers must remain aware of emerging technologies, with AI becoming a gamechanger, even as misinformation, deepfakes, and synthetically generated content pose new challenges.
He emphasised that communication must be a two-way process, with citizen feedback helping improve policies and their implementation. While speed is important, he said, accuracy and credibility remain non-negotiable, as every communication carries the authority of the institution.
He further stated that officers must continuously upgrade their skills, stay connected with the field, and be prepared to take up and understand other aspects of governance when entrusted with responsibilities beyond communication. Above all, he said, citizens must remain at the centre, with officers always asking whether their work is helping people, particularly the poorest of the poor.
