title: “Rajdharma Is a Continuing Ethic of Public Office”: Arif Mohammed Khan addresses EPFO Officers, Calls for Integrity, Empathy and Non-Discrimination in Governance
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 6:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a thought-provoking keynote at Reimagining Governance: Discourse for Excellence (RGDE), Shri Arif Mohammed Khan called for a deeper understanding of Rajdharma as an enduring ethic of public responsibility, emphasising integrity, empathy, fairness and non-discrimination in the exercise of public authority.
The session was organised by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) on 31st August 2026, under the aegis of the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security (PDUNASS), as part of the second edition of Season Two of RGDE. Senior officers and officials from EPFO and PDUNASS, along with officers from Field offices of EPFO joining virtually from across the country, participated in the session.
Rajdharma and the Responsibility of Public Power
Shri Khan reflected on the continuity and distinctiveness of Indian civilisation and described Dharma as a principle of righteous conduct and moral obligation. He emphasised that Rajdharma is ultimately concerned with the responsibility of those entrusted with public power and with the manner in which that power is exercised. He underlined the importance of non-discrimination in public life and of cultivating an approach in which the official seeks to serve rather than merely exercise authority.
He connected this ethical foundation with the inner discipline expected of a person holding public office. Referring to the spiritual idea that the Divine is present in every human being, Shri Khan stressed that an officer’s conduct should be guided by sincerity, honesty, self-restraint and a consciousness that public responsibility carries a moral dimension beyond formal procedure.
Reflecting on governance in practical terms, he stressed that rules, systems and technology are important instruments, but they cannot substitute for the human qualities that ultimately determine how citizens experience an institution. He emphasised that sincerity, cultural awareness and ethical conduct must remain at the heart of administration, particularly when officials are called upon to exercise judgement in everyday situations.
Rajdharma in the Context of Social Security
Central Provident Fund Commissioner Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi contextualised the discussion within EPFO’s responsibility for providing social security to millions of workers, pensioners and their families. He emphasised the importance of balancing legal compliance with empathy and citizen-centric service delivery as the organisation embraces technological transformation.
He highlighted the need for officers to approach their responsibilities with a spirit of selfless service, particularly while dealing with the real-life circumstances behind claims, pensions and grievances.
Civilisational Wisdom and Contemporary Governance
Director, PDUNASS, Shri Kumar Rohit, highlighted the enduring relevance of Rajdharma to contemporary public administration. Referring to the Bharat-Milap episode at Chitrakoot, he recalled how Lord Rama, while declining to return to Ayodhya, entrusted Bharata with the responsibility of governance through his Charan Padukas and imparted timeless counsel on righteous statecraft.
He emphasised that RGDE seeks to create a space where civilisational wisdom, institutional experience and contemporary administrative practice can inform one another, ultimately returning to the central purpose of public service: serving the citizen with fairness, dignity and responsibility.
Ideas to Institutional Practice
The session also featured an interactive exchange with officers, focusing on the practical application of ethical and civilisational values in everyday administration, including situations where officials must exercise judgement, balance rules with circumstances, and retain empathy while working in increasingly technology-enabled systems.
The session was moderated by Shri Prashant Sharma, RPFC-I, who facilitated the proceedings and the interaction with Shri Khan, connecting the philosophical idea of Rajdharma with the practical realities of public service.
The session concluded with expressions of gratitude to Shri Arif Mohammed Khan and the participating officers, reaffirming PDUNASS’s commitment to fostering a culture of learning, reflection and excellence in public service.

title: Indian Railways Approves ₹125 Crore Bhavnagar Para Yard Remodeling Project in Gujarat

date:

                01 SEP 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian Railways has sanctioned the Bhavnagar Para (BVP) Yard Remodeling project in Gujarat at a cost of around ₹125 crore. The project will strengthen rail infrastructure in Bhavnagar by creating additional operational capacity at Bhavnagar Para and improving facilities for passengers.
Bhavnagar Para Yard Remodeling to Ease Congestion at Bhavnagar Terminus
The project will help decongest Bhavnagar Terminus (BVC) by shifting stabling and other operational activities to Bhavnagar Para. This will enable smoother train operations, reduce rake detention and help improve punctuality. The additional infrastructure at Bhavnagar Para will facilitate better management of train movements and provide greater operational flexibility.
New Platform and Improved Passenger Facilities
The remodeling work includes four loop lines, one engine reversal line, ART and ARME siding, relocation of the Station and EI building, one high-level passenger platform, widening of the existing platform, extension of the existing Foot Over Bridge (FOB) and construction of one new FOB. The project will also include two Road Under Bridges (RUBs), including one new RUB and extension of an existing RUB, along with service buildings and associated electrical and signalling works.
Passenger convenience will be enhanced through a new high-level island platform, widening of Platform No. 2 and improved FOB connectivity at Bhavnagar Para station. These facilities will provide easier movement and access for passengers.
The Bhavnagar Para Yard Remodeling project is an important step towards strengthening railway infrastructure and improving passenger services in Bhavnagar. By easing congestion at Bhavnagar Terminus and creating additional terminal capacity, the project will support smoother and more punctual train operations. Improved platforms, FOB connectivity and other passenger facilities will further enhance convenience for people travelling to and from Bhavnagar and the surrounding region.

title: Indian Railways Approves ₹272 Crore Bypass Line Between Adra and Joychandipahar to Boost Freight Capacity
subtitle: 11 km Bypass Line to Strengthen Freight Movement and Ease Congestion
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 11:24AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian Railways has approved the construction of a 11 km bypass line between Adra end and Joychandipahar in South Eastern Railway at a total cost of ₹272 crore.
The project will provide dedicated path segregation and a bi-directional connection to the upcoming third line, facilitating projected movement of 6.065 freight rakes per day and supporting the anticipated increase in industrial traffic. The bypass will particularly support freight movement associated with SAIL’s 23.40 MTPA iron ore demand and BCCL’s projection of 45 rakes per day.
Enhancing Corridor Capacity and Reducing Congestion
The Adra-Joychandipahar-Sanka bypass will help eliminate existing operational bottlenecks and surface-crossing detentions on the Adra-Joychandipahar section. With the existing network operating at 71% utilisation and freight speeds affected by surface-crossing conflicts, the bypass will help improve operational efficiency and prevent further congestion.
The project is expected to facilitate additional traffic of 8.88 MTPA upon completion. The current line capacity of the Joychandipahar-Adra section is 47.50%, which is expected to increase to 56.45% by 2028-29.
Supporting Energy, Mineral and Cement Corridor
The bypass is part of the Energy, Mineral and Cement Corridor identified for Indian Railways. By providing additional capacity and smoother freight movement, the project will strengthen the transportation of industrial commodities and enable future traffic growth to translate into higher throughput.
The project will strengthen freight infrastructure in the Adra-Joychandipahar corridor by creating additional capacity, reducing surface-crossing conflicts and improving the efficiency of freight operations. It will support growing industrial traffic while enabling more reliable and congestion-free movement of freight on this strategically important corridor.

title: NHAI Receives Overwhelming Response from Bidders for Construction of Coastal Corridor from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha
date:

                01 SEP 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has received an overwhelming response from the bidders for the implementation of 160 km long Access Controlled Greenfield Coastal National Highway from Rameshwar to Paradeep in Odisha. Bids were invited by NHAI for construction of the project in two packages and both packages received encouraging participation from the bidders.
The 79.4 km long 4 lane access-controlled Rameshwar to Konark Package-I of the project received 10 bids, and 80.7 km long 2-lane with Paved Shoulder Konark to Paradeep Package-II received seven bids, reflecting robust competition and keen interest from the participants. The project will be awarded on Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM).
The new coastal Highway from Rameshwar to Paradeep project was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs in June 2026 with a combined total capital cost of Rs.8,300.79 crores. During construction, the project is expected to have a potential to generate 53.6 Lakhs direct man-days and 67 lakh indirect man-days of employment.
With a design speed of 100 km/hour, the project will provide direct & fast connectivity to key tourist places like Sri Jagganath Temple, Puri Beach & Konark Sun Temple and help to reduce travel time between Rameshawar and Paradeep by about 2 hours and 30 minutes.
Rameshwar-Paradeep section of Coastal Highway will offer an alternate route for NH-16 & NH-316 and improve connectivity to Puri, Konark, Paradeep Port, upcoming Puri International Airport, facilitate smooth transportation to developing ports like Astarang and Subarnarekha as well as provide connectivity to Khurda, Puri, Kendrapada and Jagatsinghpur districts in Odisha.
The existing NH-16 is part of the Golden Quadrilateral and passes through major towns of Khordha, Bhubaneswar and Cuttack. Whereas NH-316 connects Bhubaneswar to Puri and further extends towards Satapada and Konark. The current sections along Puri–Satapada and Puri–Konark stretches has nearly 40% ribbon development along the corridor with high local commuter traffic, making the corridor unsuitable for high-speed long-distance vehicular movement.
The Rameshwar-Paradeep corridor will provide faster access-controlled connectivity, reduce fuel consumption, carbon emissions & vehicle operating costs, while lowering logistics costs and supporting economic growth across the region.

title: Union Minister for Rural Development reviews progress of WDC-PMKSY; Stresses on accelerating watershed development towards 'Drought-Free India'
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today reviewed the progress of Watershed Development Component (WDC-PMKSY)  of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana and called upon the States to ensure speedy implementation of projects and clear and measurable outcomes at the grassroot level. He mentioned watershed development  as an important tool towards realizing the  goal of "Drought-Free India for Developed India".
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, "Watershed development is not just a program to build water bodies; its real objective is to bring water to the field, increase the productivity of the land, and improve the income and livelihood of the farmer. Our goal is that every drop of water should be used optimally and its benefits should reach the farmer.”
Under the WDC-PMKSY 2.0  scheme, 1,220 projects covering an area of 52.93 lakh hectares have been sanctioned so far. The total sanctioned cost of these projects is ₹12,404 crore, with ₹8,134 crore being the central share. Out of the central share, ₹6,955.75 (85%) crore has been released.
Emphasizing on the farmer-centric outcomes in particular, Union Minister of Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, "The biggest proof of the success of the watershed project is that as a result of watershed interventions, in an area of about  1.40  lakh hectares where earlier one crop was barely grown, farmers are taking two crops and in many places three crops." Horticulture, vegetable production and high-value crops have expanded which has brought prosperity in the lives of farmers. This transformation is the real success of our schemes. ”
Under the programme, 1.24 lakh water harvesting structures have been constructed and rejuvenated. These include check dams, nullahs, percolation tanks, village/farm ponds, bunds, trenches, reservoirs and other rainwater harvesting and ground water recharge structures. These structures have significantly helped in local harvesting, harvesting and recharge of ground water and increasing the availability of water for agriculture.
These efforts have resulted in protective irrigation in an additional area of 3.08 lakh hectares, helping farmers in rainfed areas to save crops in the event of deficient rainfall or drought. So far, 28.50 lakh farmers have been benefitted from the programme. In addition, afforestation, horticulture and plantation have been carried out in an area of 1.45  lakh hectares and  2.85 crore man-days employment has been generated.
Shri Chouhan urged the States to work in a transparent, tech-enabled, performance-based and people-centric manner and complete the projects in a time-bound manner. He said that watershed projects should be evaluated not only on the basis of expenditure  but also on the basis of land reclamation, water availability, irrigation, crop intensity, land productivity and actual improvement in farmers' livelihood.
Shri Chouhan said, "We have made watershed development a mass movement through 'Watershed Yatra' and 'Watershed Festival'. Now our goal is to take watershed development forward not just as a scheme, but as a national campaign for water and land security, agricultural security and rural prosperity. our resolution must  be to ensure faster implementation, better results and more impact.”
During the review meeting, the States and implementing agencies wer called to work in a coordinatedmanner to ensure that the benefits of watershed development reach the overall farmers and rural households.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Calls for Wider Awareness about Rs 1 Lakh Crore RDI Fund Among Stakeholders to Ensure Right Beneficiaries Avail of Support
subtitle:
Greater Outreach Needed to Ensure RDI Fund Reaches Technology and Research Stakeholders and Contributes to National Economic Growth

Technology Development Board Must Evolve as a Strategic Enabler of India’s Future Technology Sectors: Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 4:35PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today called for greater awareness and outreach about Rs 1 Lakh Crore “Research, Development and Innovation Fund” (RDI Fund) among stakeholders so that the right kind of applicants understand its purpose, eligibility and the process for availing support.
Addressing the 30th Foundation Day of the Technology Development Board (TDB), Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the focus should be on creating awareness about the spirit behind the RDI Fund, the stakeholders and companies eligible for support, and how they can avail of the funding. He observed that the large number of applications being received also indicated a need for greater clarity and outreach about the purpose of the Fund.
The Minister said that thousands of applications are being received, including from applicants who do not appear to understand the nature and purpose of the RDI Fund. He cautioned against the perception that the Fund is simply another source of finance or a conventional loan facility, stressing the need to ensure that there is no misunderstanding about the funding process.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the RDI Fund is intended to support technology development and research in a manner that contributes to the progress of science and research and makes these activities part of the overall growth of the national economy. He called for efforts to ensure that stakeholders understand the spirit and intended purpose of the Fund so that its benefits reach the appropriate beneficiaries.
The Minister emphasised that the funding process is already transparent and has proper safeguards in place, even though the government is open to suggestions for further safeguards wherever feasible. He said, there is scope to further increase outreach and awareness. He said that better awareness would help the right kind of people avail of the support in the interest of scientific and research progress and its contribution to national economic growth.
Referring to the role of TDB, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Board must also play a role in educating those for whom such initiatives are meant. He stressed that while technology and policy frameworks are changing rapidly, the mindset of stakeholders also needs to change accordingly.
The Minister said that TDB was created with the vision of ensuring that technologies do not remain confined to laboratories but are translated into products, solutions and enterprises that can bring ease of living to citizens, provide livelihoods and contribute to the overall economy of the country. He said that the occasion of the 30th Foundation Day was an opportunity to look back at how far this spirit had been carried forward.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that over the last 12 years this spirit had been vindicated and credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with placing science, technology and innovation high on the government agenda. He described the period as a decade of scientific renaissance in the country, highlighting achievements in science and technology and India's ability to deliver cost-effective successes.
Emphasising the importance of changing mindsets, the Minister said that continuous learning and curiosity would be essential to keeping pace with rapid technological developments. He stressed that stakeholders must make the best use of the enabling environment provided by policymakers.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the growth of the start-up ecosystem and called for prevailing myths about entrepreneurship to be dispelled. He noted that start-ups are not confined to Bengaluru or Hyderabad, that more than 50 per cent are from smaller towns, and that entrepreneurship is not necessarily restricted to young people. He also highlighted the participation of women in the ecosystem.
The Minister underlined the importance of openness to private-sector participation and said that this approach had been followed in sectors including space, biotechnology and the nuclear sector. He stressed that resource pooling and integration among institutions and stakeholders are important for strengthening the ecosystem.
Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated TDB's role in supporting the journey from laboratory to market and noted that the Board had, in practice, extended support beyond narrowly defined domains. He referred to examples including Skyroot and BotLab, and said that moving beyond a conventional bureaucratic approach had enabled TDB to become an important part of the emerging technology ecosystem.
The Minister also highlighted the need for a culture of philanthropy in research. He said that funding research that ultimately contributes to the well-being of mankind should also be recognised as a form of worship and called for such a culture to be created.
Looking ahead, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that TDB should support technology development both in the early phase and at the later stage. He noted that the RDI Fund is offering support at a later stage at TRL4 level and that TDB is the first to roll out its proposals.
He said that TDB has set up a model of public-private transition and technology self-reliance which could become an important pillar of India's economy and contribute not only to India but also to the Global South. He further observed that strengthening India's technological capabilities would also strengthen the country's geopolitical status in the Global South and across the world.
The Minister said that the first thirty years of TDB were about building the bridge between the laboratory and the market, while the next thirty years should focus on building global technology champions from India. The accompanying address similarly emphasised the need to move from ideas to innovation, from innovation to industry and towards a truly developed India by 2047.
Dr. Jitendra Singh extended his good wishes to TDB and called for the institution to continue building on its role in technology development, public-private transition and technology self-reliance.

title: “Recognise Persons with Disabilities by Their Abilities, Not Their Disability”: Dr. Virendra Kumar; Government and Social Institutions Join Hands to Take DISSSA to the Last Mile
date:

                01 SEP 2026 7:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
“Our goal must be to build an inclusive society where a person is recognised not by their disability, but by their abilities, talent, competence and potential,” said Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment, today, underscoring the need to move beyond a welfare-centric approach towards one that recognises and nurtures the capabilities and potential of persons with disabilities. He was speaking at the signing ceremony of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice Empowerment, Government of India, and the Rajyoga Education Research Foundation (RERF), a sister organisation of Brahma Kumaris, for the launch of the “Divyang Samanata, Sanrakshan evam Sashaktikaran Abhiyan (DISSSA)” at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi.
Dr. Virendra Kumar said that the empowerment of persons with disabilities cannot be achieved
through government efforts alone and requires the meaningful participation of society and the
active engagement of social, spiritual, educational and service-oriented institutions. He observed
that such partnerships can provide an effective model for taking government schemes and
services to the last mile and to those who need them most. Referring to the Rights of Persons
with Disabilities Act, 2016, he emphasised that laws and schemes can fulfill their true purpose
only when their benefits reach every eligible person in a meaningful and accessible manner. He
expressed confidence that the experience, outreach and network of RERF and its associated
organisations would contribute significantly to the empowerment of persons with disabilities. He
further stressed that when a person with a disability is empowered, the benefits extend beyond
the individual to the family, society and ultimately the nation.
Shri B.L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice & Empowerment, described the occasion as a meaningful step towards social service, equality and inclusion. He emphasised that the Government, State Governments, local administrations, families and society at large share a collective responsibility to safeguard the rights and dignity of persons with disabilities while ensuring equal opportunities for them. He said that the focus should not merely be on reducing the difficulties associated with disability, but on recognising the abilities, talents, competencies and potential of persons with disabilities and providing them opportunities to realise their full potential. He expressed confidence that the initiative would strengthen social equality, dignity and inclusion and enable persons with disabilities to participate in the mainstream of national life with confidence and equal opportunity.
Representatives of Brahma Kumaris Rajyogini BK Asha didi, Member, Brahma Kumaris
Management Committee highlighted that the organisation has been working continuously for the
empowerment of persons with disabilities, particularly children and young people, for the past 18
years. During this period, dedicated programmes and comprehensive training modules have been
developed. Two dedicated vans are used by trained teams to reach schools and colleges, with the
permission and cooperation of local authorities and educational institutions. Specially developed
educational materials, including Braille-based resources, teaching boards, games and other
training material, are used to support training, concentration, confidence-building and personality
development. National-level conferences and seminars are also organised at Mount Abu, where
persons with disabilities participate in multi-day programmes focused on empowerment and self -
reliance. The organisation expressed its appreciation to the Department for facilitating a formal
institutional partnership through the MoU, which it expects will help expand these services to a
larger number of children and young people with disabilities.
In his welcome address, Shri Rajeev Sharma, Joint Secretary, DEPwD, said that the DISSSA
initiative represents an important opportunity to complement existing government efforts with
the experience and outreach of Brahma Kumaris and RERF. He noted that under the Department’s Deendayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS), around 350–400 projects are
being supported across the country, providing education, training and rehabilitation services to
children with disabilities. He said that the expertise of the partner organisations in meditation,
Rajyoga and relaxation practices can add a valuable dimension to the holistic development of
children with disabilities by promoting mental well-being, self-confidence, concentration and
positive thinking.
The DISSSA campaign is a nationwide initiative aimed at creating an enabling environment for
Divyangjan and strengthening their equality, inclusion and empowerment. The campaign adopts
a holistic and inclusive approach that complements conventional physical, educational and
rehabilitation support by addressing important dimensions of mental and emotional well-being.
Its activities will include value-based games and motivational songs to foster happiness, positive
thinking and confidence; community meetings with parents and local communities to generate
awareness about equality and inclusion; health-awareness activities promoting de-addiction,
sanitation and cleanliness; and demonstrations and meditation sessions designed to help
Divyangjan overcome psychological barriers such as fear of failure, feelings of inferiority and
lack of confidence.

persons with different categories of disabilities, including visual, hearing, learning and

resources, community networks and the expertise of social, spiritual and educational institutions,

For students from economically marginalised families, pursuing advanced education and research can be difficult without a steady source of financial support. Timely fellowship assistance can provide the stability needed to continue academic work and progress towards a professional career.
Demonstrating the impact of support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Shri Mallela Pruthvi Raju, a 34-year-old scholar belonging to the SC-III community, overcame severe financial hardship to complete his Ph.D. and advance towards a career in scientific research.
Coming from a very poor financial background, Shri Raju had no steady income to support his education. During his academic journey, he also faced administrative hesitancy and subtle discrimination from university authorities while seeking the signatures required for the monthly and half-yearly processing of his fellowship.
Despite these difficulties, Shri Raju remained committed to his academic and professional goals. He aspired to build a successful career as a research scientist and continued preparing himself for scientific positions.
Shri Raju received fellowship assistance under the NFSC Scheme from December 2019 to December 2024. The support comprised ₹37,000 per month during the Junior Research Fellowship stage and ₹42,000 per month during the Senior Research Fellowship stage.
The fellowship became his sole financial lifeline. It transformed his circumstances from absolute financial insecurity to steady financial independence by covering his academic, research and basic living expenses.
With this support, Shri Raju was able to overcome economic hardship, remain focused on his research and successfully complete his Ph.D.
Shri Raju is currently working as a Project Scientist at HCU. He continues to prepare for scientific positions and is progressing towards his long-term aspiration of establishing himself as a full-time research scientist.
The NFSC Scheme helped transform a period of severe financial strain into one of academic achievement and professional advancement. The fellowship enabled him to complete advanced education without abandoning his research ambitions.
His academic perseverance also resulted in the publication of three research papers, reflecting his continued engagement with scientific research.

He added that every generation must walk together for the nation to move forward, which is the true spirit of ‘
Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas.’
Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B.L. Verma said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, our government remains committed to strengthening family bonds across the country. title: From Financial Hardship to Sanitation Entrepreneurship: Chetan Kumar Kaushik's Journey towards Self-Reliance under NAMASTE-SUY

content:
Chetan Kumar Kaushik, a 32-year-old resident of Sahibabad in Ghaziabad district, Uttar Pradesh, has transformed years of financial hardship into a journey of self-reliance and dignity. Educated up to the 12th standard, Chetan provides sewer and septic tank suction services in the Mohan Nagar and Sahibabad areas under Nagar Nigam Ghaziabad's Mohan Nagar Zone.
For years, sanitation-related work remained Chetan's primary source of livelihood. Despite working continuously, his limited earnings were largely spent on household expenses and family responsibilities, leaving little scope for savings, business expansion or long-term financial security.
His difficulties increased when his mother became seriously ill and required prolonged medical care. As the sole earning member of the family, Chetan bore the responsibility of supporting his homemaker wife and arranging his mother's treatment. He used the savings generated through his sanitation work to secure treatment for her at reputed hospitals. Despite his efforts, his mother passed away in 2022. The experience was both emotionally devastating and financially demanding, but Chetan continued to fulfil his responsibilities with determination.
A decisive change came through the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) component of the NAMASTE scheme. Chetan received financial assistance, including an upfront capital subsidy, to strengthen and expand his sanitation service enterprise.
The project, with a total cost of
Rs. 8.90 lakh
, was supported through a loan of
Rs. 5,42,500
and a capital subsidy of
Rs. 3,47,500
. The assistance enabled him to strengthen his suction-machine operations and provide improved sanitation services across areas under the Mohan Nagar Zone.
With better equipment and an expanded livelihood base, Chetan's monthly income increased to approximately
Rs. 40,000-Rs. 50,000
. The intervention brought greater stability to his household finances, enhanced his capacity to meet family responsibilities and helped him move towards financial independence.
Chetan currently pays a monthly loan instalment of
Rs. 12,100
. With only around
Rs. 67,000
remaining outstanding, he expects to repay the loan fully by
October 2026
.
Today, Chetan continues to operate his sanitation service enterprise successfully. The scheme has not only improved his income but also strengthened his confidence, independence and social dignity.
His journey demonstrates how timely financial assistance and livelihood support can help sanitation workers overcome economic barriers and build sustainable enterprises. Through resilience, hard work and support under NAMASTE-SUY, Chetan has emerged as an inspiring example of sanitation entrepreneurship and self-reliance.
The assistance released on 14 September 2021 reflects the Government's commitment to promoting financial inclusion, improving livelihood opportunities and empowering sanitation workers through safe and sustainable entrepreneurship.

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development

                01 SEP 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, has launched the theme for Adoption Awareness 2026, reinforcing its commitment to promoting legal, safe, transparent and child-centric adoption across the country.
The theme for Adoption Awareness 2026 is:
Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future.
Say No to Illegal Adoption!
The theme was formally launched by Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA, during a Live Morning Show on DD National, marking the beginning of a sustained nationwide awareness initiative to promote legal adoption and prevent illegal adoption practices.
During the programme, Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA, emphasised the importance of following the legal adoption process and said, “Adoption is not a shortcut—it is a sacred responsibility. Through CARA and the legally prescribed channels, we safeguard the dignity, rights and future of every orphaned, abandoned or surrendered child. Every child deserves a safe, loving and secure family—not secrecy, uncertainty or risk.”
CARA has been undertaking several measures to strengthen awareness, coordination and enforcement against illegal adoption practices, including enhanced coordination with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Ministry of Home Affairs. However, sustained awareness and capacity building at the State, district and community levels remain critical to ensuring that every child is protected and every adoption is carried out through the prescribed legal process.
Year-Round Outreach to Promote Legal Adoption
Under the theme “Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future. Say No to Illegal Adoption,” several outreach activities will be conducted throughout the year to create widespread awareness among citizens and key stakeholders.
As part of the initiative, State/UT-level Adoption Awareness Workshops are being organised from September 2026 onwards, moving beyond the earlier approach of limiting adoption awareness activities to the month of November. These workshops will provide a platform for stakeholders to understand the statutory adoption process, strengthen inter-departmental coordination, identify and address illegal adoption practices, and reinforce the principle of the best interest of the child.
The campaign will involve a wide range of stakeholders, including Women and Child Development Departments, Child Welfare Committees, District Child Protection Units, Specialised Adoption Agencies, Child Care Institutions, Police, Health Departments, Judiciary, Legal Services Authorities, hospitals and nursing homes, medical professionals, ASHA and ANM workers, civil society organisations, media and digital platforms, among others.
Adoption Awareness Workshop in Delhi on 10 September 2026
As part of this nationwide initiative, CARA will organise an Adoption Awareness Workshop in Delhi on Thursday, 10 September 2026, at the Delhi Secretariat, New Delhi in collaboration of Department of Women and Child Development, Govt. of Delhi and concerned authorities.
The workshop will focus on strengthening awareness regarding the legal adoption framework and the roles and responsibilities of stakeholders in ensuring that children in need of care and protection receive appropriate care, protection and rehabilitation through lawful mechanisms.
The workshop will also emphasise the importance of timely reporting of children found separated from their guardians, lawful surrender procedures, declaration of children as legally free for adoption, and adherence to the prescribed adoption procedure.
A Collective Responsibility to Protect Every Child
The campaign seeks to ensure that prospective adoptive parents and the general public understand that adoption is a legal and child-centric process—not a private arrangement between individuals.
Citizens are encouraged to follow only the legally prescribed adoption process through CARA and the designated authorities/agencies and to report suspected instances of illegal adoption to the competent authorities.
Through sustained, year-round awareness and coordinated action, CARA aims to build a stronger ecosystem in which every child’s dignity, identity, rights, safety and future are protected.

title: From Awareness to Ownership
subtitle: Building a People's Movement for River Conservation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
For centuries, the Ganga has been woven into India’s civilisation, culture and everyday life.
It has nurtured communities, supported livelihoods and inspired traditions across generations. Over time, however, growing cities, pollution and unplanned urbanisation placed increasing pressure on the river. This highlighted the need to strengthen its ecological health and people’s relationship with it. Reviving the Ganga, therefore, calls for more than cleaning its water. This broader understanding shapes the
Namami Gange Programme (NGP)
, launched in 2014.
The programme is an Integrated Conservation Mission for the Ganga and its tributaries. It brings together pollution abatement, conservation and river rejuvenation. NGP’s work extends across sewage treatment, riverfront development, afforestation, etc. Scientific monitoring and public awareness further strengthen this integrated effort. Yet, lasting transformation depends on a partner that no programme can do without. That partner is the community itself. This belief gave rise to
Jan Ganga
, the public participation pillar of Namami Gange. Inspired by the vision of
Jan Bhagidari
, it places people at the centre of conservation. This is where Namami Gange becomes a story of people. A story that moves from awareness to participation, and ultimately towards ownership.
United by the River: Celebrating Stories of Participation
A river can bring people together in ways that extend beyond environmental action. Its banks become spaces where communities meet, participate and celebrate their shared connection. Jan Ganga creates such opportunities through cleanliness drives, plantation campaigns and educational initiatives. These activities turn conservation into a collective experience rather than an isolated responsibility.
One of the clearest expressions of this participation under NGP is river cleanliness. The
Ganga Swachhta Pakhwada
has become an important platform for spreading this message. Observed annually from
16th to 31st March
, it is a fortnight-long event that reaches thousands of people across the five main-stem Ganga basin States. These include
Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal
. It also covers the
National Capital Territory of Delhi
and towns along Ganga’s tributaries. Students, volunteers, community groups and other stakeholders participate in coordinated efforts to strengthen public engagement with river conservation.
This momentum is further sustained through regular weekly cleanliness drives along the
Yamuna
in Delhi. These drives contribute directly to cleaner river stretches and surrounding areas. Together, such efforts are helping make river conservation a regular civic practice rather than an activity limited to designated occasions.
As communities care for cleaner river stretches, their attention also extends to riverbanks. Plantation has consequently become an integral part of public participation under Namami Gange. Healthy vegetation helps stabilise riverbanks and reduce soil erosion. These ecological benefits strengthen the resilience of rivers and their surrounding habitats.
Complementing this, the
‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’
campaign has deepened participation in plantation activities. The campaign encourages people to plant trees as heartfelt tributes to their mothers. It also connects personal emotion with a shared responsibility towards environmental conservation. The powerful connection has encouraged individuals, families and communities to participate with renewed purpose. This spirit is also reflected in the way
World Environment Day
brings citizens together. Through plantation drives, awareness activities and community initiatives, the occasion further strengthens public participation in environmental conservation.
A movement also becomes stronger when its values reach the next generation. This makes youth engagement an important part of Jan Ganga. Schools, colleges and universities now offer diverse avenues for environmental learning and creative expression. Students explore river-related themes through essays, paintings, posters, debates and interactive awareness programmes.
Experiential activities provide opportunities to connect classroom knowledge with real-world ecological challenges.
University Ganga Clubs
extend this involvement through lectures, field visits, volunteering and outreach initiatives. Eco-clubs, NCC units and educational institutions provide additional platforms for sustained participation. Together, these efforts foster informed young citizens committed to protecting rivers beyond textbooks and classrooms.
The Namami Gange Programme has integrated river conservation into several annual observances.
These occasions keep people connected with rivers throughout the year. Among them,
Ganga Utsav
stands out as a flagship platform for community engagement. It commemorates the Ganga’s recognition as
India’s National River
. This brings together performances, exhibitions, art contests and public dialogues, creating spaces for participation and shared expression. Other observances, including
Swachhta Hi Seva
and
International Day of Yoga,
further expand opportunities for public involvement. They reinforce the enduring cultural relationship between people and rivers.
A deeper connection with rivers often emerges through direct experience rather than awareness alone. The Namami Gange Programme has created innovative initiatives to bring the spirit of river conservation into public life. A notable example was the
Border Security Force’s all-women river rafting expedition
along the Ganga. The journey covered the river from its upper reaches to the sea, showcasing courage, collaboration and environmental commitment. It presented the Ganga as more than a natural resource. Interactions with students, residents and young volunteers created spaces for conversation.
Across the Ganga basin,
Ganga Praharis
have become committed community volunteers supporting conservation efforts at the grassroots. They work with residents to spread environmental awareness, encourage responsible practices and safeguard local biodiversity.
Ganga Seva Doots
complement these efforts by extending outreach across schools, institutions and neighbourhoods. Through awareness drives and local initiatives, they help bring river conservation closer to everyday community life. Protecting aquatic life, restoring habitats and maintaining ecological balance further strengthens people’s connection with the river. Together, these volunteer networks reflect the
spirit of Jan Bhagidari
through citizen-led action. Their efforts demonstrate how informed communities can become enduring guardians of rivers and their surrounding ecosystems.
Creating a Culture of River Stewardship
The most lasting legacy of river rejuvenation is not only a healthier river, but a stronger relationship with it. Infrastructure can restore river health, scientific interventions can strengthen ecosystems and technology can improve monitoring and management. Yet the long-term future of rivers depends upon something that cannot be created through engineering alone. Through Jan Ganga, the Namami Gange Programme has demonstrated that each effort contributes to a larger transformation.  It is far more than an environmental mission. Guided by the vision of Jan Bhagidari, it shows how collective action can become the foundation of sustainable development.

India’s sovereign credit assessment further reflects this confidence. In August 2026, S&P Global Ratings affirmed India’s
‘BBB/A-2’ sovereign ratings with a Stable Outlook
. This followed the upgrade of its long-term rating to ‘BBB’ in 2025, after an 18-year gap.
A Stronger Start to 2026-27

7.0%
for the quarter.

in Q1 FY 2026-27.  It recorded

in Q1 FY 2025-26.

, or GDP at Current Prices, is estimated at
₹88.27 lakh crore
.  It recorded
10.3% rise
, compared with 8.1% last year.
Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
is the value of final goods and services produced in the domestic economy in an accounting period.
Real GVA
is estimated at
₹73.82 lakh crore
, recording
8.2% growth
, compared with 7.0% last year.

is estimated at
₹80.53 lakh crore
, recording
11.5% growth
, compared with 8.1% last year.
Gross Value Added (GVA)
measures the individual contribution of producers, industries or sectors to the economy.

Recent Indicators Signal Continued Momentum

Recent Policy Measures Supporting Growth
Policy measures introduced during 2026 have complemented these economic trends, spanning manufacturing, energy security, trade and investment, and agriculture.
Manufacturing and Industry
The
Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme
(July 2026) has an outlay of
₹62,500 crore through 2030-31.
It aims to further expand production, deepen value addition and strengthen global competitiveness.
Approved in July 2026,
Semicon 2.0
has a budget outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore. It supports chip design and manufacturing, advanced packaging, research, materials, equipment and talent development.
Approved in July 2026, the
BHAVYA Rasayan Scheme
has an outlay of ₹3,030 crore for a period of 5 years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. It will support the establishment of three dedicated chemical parks across the country.
Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme 5.0 (ECLGS 5.0)
targets additional credit flow of ₹2.55 lakh crore in response to the West Asia situation. It provides 100% guarantee coverage for MSMEs and 90% for non-MSMEs.
Passed by Parliament in
August 2026
, the
MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026
simplifies compliance and supports MSME development and competitiveness.
Energy Security
Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme,
has an outlay of ₹84,084 crore through FY 2030-31. The Scheme supports exploration to unlock India’s offshore energy potential.
The
Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects
was approved in
May 2026
with an outlay of
₹37,500 crore
. It supports the
100 MT coal gasification target by 2030
and aims to reduce import dependence.
GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme
, was approved in
August 2026
with an outlay of
₹23,731 crore
. The Scheme will be implemented from
FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36
. It aims to increase compressed biogas production from agricultural, animal and municipal organic waste.
Approved in July 2026,
Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)
has an outlay of ₹5,070 crore. It supports
5,000 MW
of floating solar projects with co-located energy storage, with projects sanctioned during FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
Trade and Investment
The India-UK CETA and Agreement on Social Security
entered into force on 15 July 2026. It provides zero-duty access for nearly 99% of India’s exports to the UK.
The India-Israel Bilateral Investment Agreement (BIA)
entered into force on 4 July 2026. It aims to strengthen bilateral economic ties and provides a more secure and predictable framework for investment.
In June 2026, reforms were announced to
expand Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) participation in Government Securities
. Key measures include tax exemptions, wider coverage under the Fully Accessible Route and streamlined investment norms. The reforms are intended to attract long-term foreign capital and deepen India’s debt market.
Launched in
May 2026
, the
Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)
carries a sovereign guarantee of
₹12,980 crore
. It provides maritime risk cover while reducing dependence on foreign insurers amid global volatility.
Agriculture: Farm Income and Production Support
The continuation of
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 has been approved with an outlay of ₹3.15 lakh crore. The scheme provides eligible farmer families income support through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system.
For
Marketing Season 2026-27
, the Government increased MSPs for
14 Kharif crops
to ensure remunerative prices for farmers. The highest absolute increases were for
sunflower seed, cotton, nigerseed and sesamum
.
Approved in May 2026, the
Mission for Cotton Productivity (Kapas Kanti)
has an outlay of ₹5,659.22 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31. It links cotton farmers with modern research and technologies, reduces pest risks, and strengthens production systems and agricultural trade.
The
National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 (NIPU-2026)
aims to promote new investment in gas-based urea manufacturing units. It supports higher domestic production and India’s goal of self-sufficiency in urea.
These measures build on a decade of policy initiatives including Make in India, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, PM-KISAN, the Export Promotion Mission and others.
Conclusion
India’s economic performance at the start of 2026-27 reflects
broad-based momentum across key areas of the economy.
Investment has accelerated, household consumption has remained firm, while manufacturing, services and exports have provided additional support.
More recent indicators show that this strength has carried beyond the first quarter. Continued government support through various policy measures has also helped maintain the pace of economic activity.

date:

                01 SEP 2026 9:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved acquisition of up to 100% equity shareholding of Apollo Fertility Centre Pvt. Ltd (AFCPL) and Apollo Specialty Hospitals Pvt. Ltd. (ASHPL) by Kids Clinic India Ltd. (KCIL) and related transactions.
The proposed combination involves:
acquisition of up to 100% equity shareholding of AFCPL, and 100% equity shareholding of ASHPL by KCIL (
Proposed Apollo Acquisition
);
issuance of equity shares and optionally convertible debentures, representing 9.9% shareholding in KCIL (on a fully diluted basis) to Apollo Health and Lifestyle Limited (
AHLL
) in part consideration for the Proposed Apollo Acquisition (
Proposed KCIL Acquisition
); and
issuance of certain equity shareholding in KCIL to Arvon Investments Pte. Ltd. (
Arvon
) (
Proposed KCIL Investment
).
(The aforementioned steps are collectively referred to as the ‘
Proposed Combination
’).
KCIL is a public limited company operating chains of super-specialty hospitals under the brand ‘Cloudnine’, focused on mother and baby care, and operates across the verticals of maternity, gynaecology, paediatrics, and fertility. It currently operates centres across multiple cities in India, including Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Hyderabad, Lucknow, Ludhiana and Chandigarh.
AHLL also operates in the healthcare space, by way of operating primary care clinics and diagnostic services. Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited (
AHEL
) holds 100% equity shareholding in AHLL. AHEL is a publicly listed company with the promoter group holding 28.02% shareholding, and the public shareholders hold the remaining 71.98% shareholding.
AFCPL is a chain of fertility clinics under the Apollo Group and is entirely held by AHLL. It specializes in assisted reproductive treatments and reproductive medicine, offering services such as In vitro fertilisation (
IVF
), embryo freezing, genetic testing
etc
.
ASHPL had three business segments namely Cradle, Fertility and Spectra till June 2024.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sexual assault of a minor girl by a bus driver and conductor in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh
subtitle:
Issues notices to Police Commissioners of Delhi and Gautam Budh Nagar and Mainpuri Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

The report expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the victim
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that a 16-year-old girl was subjected to gang rape by a driver and a conductor of a bus that she boarded from Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh on 4th August 2026. Reportedly, the perpetrators extended life threats and left her at the Kashmere Gate Bus Terminal in Delhi.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of human rights violations. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Police Commissioners of Delhi and Gautam Budh Nagar and Mainpuri Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation and compensation, if any, paid to the victim.
According to the media report, carried on 31
st
August 2026, the girl left home in Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh to visit her cousin in Sector 63, but she missed her stop and alighted at Pari Chowk. From there, she reportedly boarded another bus after confirming that it was going to Sector 63 of Noida.

The online quiz will be available till 10th October 2026 on MyGov platform. It is open to all Indian citizens aged 14 and above.

title: Swachhata Pakhwada-2026 Begins in Department of Fertilizers with Message from Union Minister Shri J. P. Nadda
subtitle:
Officials and Employees of the Department Take Swachhata Pledge Under the Leadership of Secretary, Shri Rajat Kumar Mishra

Department Officials and Employees Reaffirm Their Commitment to Cleanliness and a Clean Work Culture
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Fertilizers
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                01 SEP 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Swachhata Pakhwada-2026 commenced in the Department of Fertilizers, Government of India, with a message from the Hon’ble Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri J. P. Nadda. In his message, the Hon’ble Minister described Swachhata Pakhwada as an important nationwide initiative towards building a clean, green and sustainable India.
In his message, the Hon’ble Minister said, “Swachhata Pakhwada is a nationwide initiative that reflects our vision of a clean, green and sustainable India and strengthens our collective commitment to maintaining clean and healthy workplaces and surrounding environments, in line with the objectives of Swachh Bharat.”
He called upon all officers and employees to actively participate in the cleanliness campaign and contribute towards making its observance successful and meaningful. He also extended his best wishes for the successful conduct of Swachhata Pakhwada-2026.
Following the Hon’ble Minister’s message, officials and employees of the Department of Fertilizers took the Swachhata Pledge under the leadership of Shri Rajat Kumar Mishra, Secretary, Department of Fertilizers, Government of India.
On the occasion, the Secretary called upon all officers and employees to extend active cooperation towards the cleanliness initiative. He stated that cleanliness is not merely a campaign but a moral responsibility and it is the responsibility of every individual to uphold it. He urged everyone to maintain cleanliness at their workplace and in the surrounding environment and to make cleanliness an integral part of their daily work culture.
The officials and employees of the Department participated enthusiastically in the Swachhata Pledge programme and resolved to discharge their responsibilities towards cleanliness with sincerity and dedication. They also expressed their commitment to creating a clean and healthy office environment, enhancing awareness about cleanliness and keeping their workplaces neat and clean.
The Department of Fertilizers is observing Swachhata Pakhwada-2026 from 1st to 15th September 2026. During the Pakhwada, various activities are being organised to promote cleanliness, environmental protection, digital cleanliness and a clean work culture.
